## Investigation

Which physical device and macOS host are being observed, before any setting,
firmware, or software state is changed?

::: {.manual-prereq title="Protect the starting state"}

Use one Seaboard Block and the M4 MacBook Pro. Do not open ROLI Dashboard, run
an updater, change a device setting, or flash firmware. Keep the device
disconnected while you create the record. Confirm that an intention
specification under `../specs/` selects the preservation-investigation route and
is marked `ready to run`.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Create private and reviewable records"}

From the repository root, copy the two templates:

```bash
cp evidence/templates/device-identity.private.yml evidence/private/seaboard-block-01.yml
cp evidence/templates/device-baseline.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-baseline.yml
```

Put serial number and Bluetooth address only in the private record. In the
reviewable baseline, record the date, macOS version, Mac model, device label,
connection planned for the test, and the fact that no device state has been
changed.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Record visible version information"}

If a version label is visible on the device, packaging, or a previously saved
legitimate record, transcribe it as *reported*, with its source. Do not launch
vendor software solely to discover a version at this stage. Leave unknown fields
as `unknown`; unknown is useful evidence.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Evaluate the baseline record"}

This stage passes when both records exist, the private record remains outside
Git, and the reviewable baseline identifies one device and one host without
claiming any MIDI or MPE result. It is acceptable—and expected—for firmware and
other fields to remain `unknown`.

If any setting was changed or an updater was opened, mark the baseline as
`contaminated`, explain why, and begin again with the next untouched device.

:::
